 ORDER

The complainant filed the present Civil Contempt Petition under the provisions ofe d Sections 11 and 12 of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, against the accused, alleging willful disobedience of the Order dated 12.08.2014 passed in W.P.No. 28013/2014, wherein, the learned single Judge, at paragraph 5, held as under:
"5.
Hence, to consider these aspects of the matter, the representation/notice dated 09.10.2013 should have to be noticed by the respondent Nos.1 and 2 and appropriate decision be taken in the matter.
To enable the same, the petitioner shall now file one more copy of the representation/notice with the 2nd respondent within four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this Order.
The same shall be examined and the result of the consideration shall be intimated to the petitioner in an expeditious manner, but not later than two months thereon.
Needless to mention that if the decision taken by the 2nd respondent is to transmit the amount to the Civil Court, the said transmission shall also be completed.

If any other person is to be notified before a decision be taken by the 2nd respondent, the same shall also be complied and thereafter decision be taken."
2. Since the respondents failed to comply with the said order, the petitioner was forced to file CCC No.414/2016 before this Court.

When the said contempt petition was listed on 05.07.2016, on the prayer made by the learned counsel for the complainant seeking permission to withdraw the contempt petition, the co-ordinate Bench of this Court, dismissed the contempt petition as withdrawn, with liberty to the complainant to approach this Court in future, if need be, as per law.
3. In spite of the assurance given, the accused did not pass the award within the time stipulated.
Thereby, again, the complainant was forced to file the second contempt petition i.e., present contempt petition on 16.01.2019.
In response to the notice on 03.11.2022, the accused persons entered appearance.

On 29.11.2022, this Court, passed a detailed Order, wherein, at paragraphs 5 to 8, it was observed under:
"5. We are not happy with the affidavit filed by B.D.A. in compliance of the order passed by the learned Single Judge.
The learned Single Judge directed the accused-B.D.A. to examine and the result of consideration shall be intimated to the petitioner in expeditious manner, but not later than two months thereon.
In spite of the order having been passed for more than eight years back, the accused has not raised the occasion to implement the order within the time stipulated.
Only after the present contempt petition was filed on 16.01.2019 and after issuance of notice by this Court and, that too, after several hearing dates, affidavit has been filed on 29.11.2022,

The Commissioner, B.D.A., is hereby directed to be present before the Court, on the next date of hearing, to hear before framing of charges.

8. List this matter on 06.12.2022"
4.

Thereafter, on 06.12.2022, an application came to be filed seeking exemption from personal appearance of the Commissioner, BDA, which was rejected directing the Commissioner to be present on 08.12.2022 'to hear and frame charge'.

On the said date, Sri Kumar Naik, Commissioner,
BDA, appeared before the Court and submitted that though necessary steps have been taken, they could not comply the order and sought time to apply his mind and come back to the Court.

5. Subsequently, when the matter was listed on 03.01.2023, Sri Murugesh V. Charati, learned counsel for the accused, on instructions from Dr.B.S.Basanthi, Additional Special Land Acquisition Officer, BDA, submitted that draft order is ready and within ten days, final award would be passed.
That is how the matter is posted today.

6. Today, Sri Murugesh V. Charati, learned counsel for the BDA filed the Memo dated 12.01.2023 along with the award dated 06.01.2023 passed in respect of land in Sy.No.108 of Kalathammanahalli village, Hesaraghatta Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, approved on 10.01.2023 and the notice under Section 12(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, dated 11.01.2023 informing about the award.
The Memo along with documents is placed on record.
7. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties to the lis.

8. Sri Santhosh, learned counsel for Sri Varadarajan, M.S., learned counsel for the complainants contended that even though the learned single Judge passed the Order as long back as on 12.08.2014 directing the accused to consider the petitioner's representation in an expeditious manner, but not later than two months thereon, it was not complied within the time stipulated.
Thereby, the complainant was forced for file CCC No.414/2016.
However, on the assurance given by the accused to pass award and issue notice, the complainant withdrew the contempt petition on 05.07.2016.
Liberty was reserved to the complainant to approach this Court in future if need be, as per law.
However, the accused persons did not pass any award.
Thereby, the complainant was forced to file the present contempt petition on 16.01.2019.
Even after filing of the present contempt petition, in spite of granting sufficient opportunity, the accused did not comply with the order.

At last, when this Court took a serious view on the conduct and attitude of the accused, under the fear of being punished in the contempt, the accused have now passed the award, after lapse of nearly 8 years 4 months.
Thereby, complainants have been dragged to the Court, two times in contempt petition by spending their precious time, litigation expenses and undergoing mental trauma.

Therefore, learned counsel for the complainants submits that the contempt petition may be Balavendra vs Sri. G.Kumar Naik on 12 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62402843/
4 disposed off imposing exemplary costs on the accused.
9.
Sri M.V.Charati, learned counsel for the BDA has not disputed the fact that CCC No.414/2016 filed earlier was withdrawn by the complainant on the assurance given by the BDA to pass award.

Since the present Commissioner was not there as on the date of the Order passed by the learned single Judge and subsequently, many Commissioners were transferred, it was not possible to pass the award within the stipulated time.

It is contended that, the present Commissioner has made in serious efforts and passed the award and same was communicated to the complainant by issuing notice under Section 12(2) of the Land Acquisition Act.
Thereby, the Order passed by the learned single Judge has been complied with and therefore, sought to drop the contempt proceedings.

10. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, it is undisputed fact that the learned single Judge passed the order as long back as on 12.08.2014 in W.P.No.28013/2014 permitting the petitioner to make representation and directing the BDA to examine the same and intimate the result of such consideration to the petitioner in an expeditious manner, but not later than two months thereon.
Unfortunately, the accused- BDA has not done such an exercise within the time stipulated.

Thereby, the complainant was forced to file CCC No.414/2016 and on the assurance given by the learned counsel for the BDA that award will be passed and award notice will be issued at the earliest, the said contempt petition was dismissed as withdrawn on 05.07.2016 with liberty to the complainant to approach this Court in future, if need be, as per law.
11. In spite of the same, since accused-BDA failed to comply with the order passed by the learned single Judge, the complainant was forced to file the present contempt petition on 16.01.2019.
The order sheet maintained in the present contempt petition clearly depicts that in spite of repeated orders, the accused-BDA has shown lethargic attitude in complying with the order.
In terms of the order dated 12.08.2014 passed in W.P.No.28013/2014, the petitioner made representation on 04.09.2014.
Therefore, the BDA ought to - 10 - have considered the representation on or before 04.11.2014.
Unfortunately, in spite of filing of the earlier contempt and the present contempt petition, the accused-BDA has not opened its eyes.
Even after filing of the present contempt petition on 16.01.2019, the matter was dragged till today, i.e., for more than four years.

12. This Court took serious note of the lapse on the part of the accused-BDA and passed the detailed order dated 29.11.2022, which reads as under:
"It is yet another unfortunate case listed today for not complying with the order passed by the learned Single Judge, even after lapse of eight years.
2.

No.108 of Kalathammana halli Village, Hesaraghatta Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk and has been notified for acquisition proceedings along with other lands.
Thereafter the Bangalore Development Authority has not passed award in respect of any of the properties notified for the formation of Peripheral Ring Road Part-I.
The possession of the properties is also not taken over by the Bangalore Development Authority.

The acquisition proceedings pertaining to the Peripheral Ring Road were challenged by several land owners before this Hon'ble Court and at present the acquisition proceedings are pending consideration before the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has issued several interim directions to the Bangalore Development Authority as well as to the State Government.

The Bangalore Development Authority has addressed a letter to the State Government seeking instructions/directions from the State Government with regard to the process of determination of compensation and passing of the awards.
The State Government is yet to issue instructions/directions to the Bangalore Development Authority.

I submit that once the instructions/directions are received from the State Government, the - 13 - process of determination of compensation, passing of awards would be commenced by the Additional Land Acquisition Officer of Bangalore Development Authority.

During the course of determination of the compensation and entitlement in the award proceedings, suitable action in accordance with law would be taken and the same would be intimated to the Complainant.

7. I once again submit and reiterate that the Bangalore Development Authority has not passed any award in respect of the lands notified for the formation of Peripheral Ring Road Oara-1 till today and is awaiting the Instructions/directions from the State Government.
8. I submit that the order passed by the Learned Single Judge has been complied.
I submit that I have not disobeyed the order passed by this Hon'ble Court.

4. On perusal of Annexure-R1 endorsement dated 23-11- 2022, B.D.A. has not complied with the order, but it has stated that the compensation with regard to Peripheral Ring Road Part-I, the State Government is yet to issue instructions/directions to B.D.A. and once the order is issued from the Government, they will verify the records and sanction compensation to the actual owner.
5.

forthwith."

13. Now, Sri M.V.Charati, learned counsel for the accused- BDA has filed the Memo dated 12.01.2023 enclosing therewith copy of the award dated 06.01.2023 passed in respect of land in Sy.No.108 of Kalathammanahalli village, Hesaraghatta Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, approved on 10.01.2023 and the award notice dated 11.01.2023 under Section 12(2) of the Land Acquisition Act,
informing the award.
Thereby, the order of the learned single Judge has been complied with after lapse of more than 8 years, that too, after filing two contempt petitions.
This clearly indicates that the accused has no respect to the Court Order.
14. The complainants approached this Court with great expectations.
Today, the judiciary is repository of public faith.
It is the trustee of the people.
It is last hope of the people.
After every knock at all the doors fail people approach the judiciary as the last resort.
It is the only temple worshipped by - 16 - every citizen of this nation, regardless of religion, caste, sex or place of birth.
15. It is the duty of the accused-BDA to pass the order with the time stipulated.
For any reason, if the Order could not be passed, they should have approached the learned single Judge seeking extension of time.
Since the same has not been done, and since no appeal has been filed, the order passed by the learned single Judge has reached finality.
The accused-BDA has shown lethargic attitude in implementing the Court Order, thereby, indirectly made mockery of justice and it is nothing but interference with the administration of justice.
It is well settled that the authorities like BDA are under constitutional duty coupled with power.

Every officer of the BDA or any other public servant is a trustee of the society and in all facets of public administration, every public servant has to exhibit honesty, integrity, sincerity and faithfulness in implementation of the political, social,
economic and constitutional policies to integrate the nation, to achieve excellence and efficiency in the public administration.
The conduct of the accused is in utter - 17 - violation of the Articles 14, 21 and 300A of the Constitution of India.
16. The accused have unnecessarily dragged the complainants to the Court.
Though the complainants succeeded before the learned single Judge, they were made to file two contempt petitions for implementation of the order.
This is nothing but interference with the administration of justice.
The accused have constantly harassed the complainants for more than eight years, though they succeeded before the learned single Judge.
Thereby, the complainants were made to undergo mental trauma and suffer financial loss.

Finally, the accused have complied with the Order, in view Balavendra vs Sri. G.Kumar Naik on 12 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62402843/
8 of the threat of contempt.

Therefore, the accused-BDA has to pay costs quantified at Rs.1,00,000/-
(Rupees one lakh only) for delay of more than 8 years in complying with the order passed by the learned single Judge.
17. Sri M.V.Charati, learned counsel for the accused-BDA submitted that proper address of the complainants has to be provided to the authority.
Accordingly, the learned counsel for the complainants furnished the addresses of the complainants - 18 - to the learned counsel for the accused, in the open Court, today.

18. In view of the above, we pass the following:
ORDER (i) The contempt proceedings are hereby dropped, subject to accused paying costs of Rs.1,00,000/- from their pocket (i.e., Rs.50,000/- to the complainants and Rs.50,000/- to the Bengaluru Advocates' Association, which shall be utilized towards development of Library), within a period of two weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Order and produce the acknowledgment.
(ii) It is needless to observe that, if the complainants are not happy with the award passed by the accused, it is open for the complainants to pursue their remedy, in accordance with law.
In view of disposal of the contempt petition, all pending applications shall stand disposed off.
